newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Study finds Cambodia sex discrimination rampant.
newsitem.headline: Study finds Cambodia sex discrimination rampant.

text.p: While an estimated 70 percent of Cambodia's work force is composed of women, few females reach management positions, making Cambodia one of Asia's most sexist work places, according to a newly released labour study.

"Working women in Cambodia," a report from the Asian American Free Labor Institute (AAFLI), found that economic gains in the Southeast Asian nation are being undermined by deteriorating workers' rights for women.
"So many women in Cambodia are their family's bread-winner," AAFLI official Bama Aretheya said on Monday. "But women are not advancing."
The causes for women's plight include the toll of more than 20 years of civil war and the large number who have been abandoned by their husbands, the official said.
The report said men, who compose 45 percent of the general population and a suprisingly low 30 percent of the work force, are promoted more often and routinely paid more for the same work.

"In the construction industry, employers tell women workers that they are not entitled to earn as much as men for the same jobs because they are not as strong as men, and therefore cannot work as hard," it noted.
In the manufacturing industry, employers were said to favour young, unmarried women for low-level jobs because they tended to be less aware of their rights.
The study querried 1,000 people in Phnom Penh and four rural regions and conducted 25 in-depth interviews.
